title: Implement backpressure gossip protocol and upgrade Netty/Redis clients
creator: Asha Menon
description:
Problem: During multi-tenant spikes we observe head-of-line latency amplification when one downstream service slows. Existing propagation uses a centralized lease/coordination hop which adds contention and increases tail latency. Additionally, several Redis/Kafka client versions in the async pipeline are out of date; known bugs in our current Lettuce/Netty combination surface under high connection churn and exacerbate GC pressure.

Goal: Introduce a lightweight, peer-to-peer 'backpressure gossip' mechanism so ingress shards exchange localized pressure signals and shed or slow non-critical work earlier. In parallel, bump Netty and Redis/Kafka client libraries to versions with connection/leak fixes and improved IO backpressure primitives.

Non-goals: This ticket does not change routing policies or tenant prioritization rules; it focuses on signal propagation and client hardening. Full end-to-end rate-limiting policy changes will be follow-ups.

Approach:
- Design a compact pressure signal format (tenant, shard, token-rate, ttl) and piggyback it on existing heartbeat/lease messages to avoid a new RPC.
- Implement a local hysteresis controller per ingress shard that consumes gossip signals and translates them into a score that adjusts local queue admission and consumer credit.
- Add a governance layer to prefer observed queue-dropping over synchronous head-of-line blocking (graceful shed).
- Replace Lettuce 5.x with Lettuce 6.x (or equivalent) and Netty 4.1.92 -> 4.1.100; upgrade Kafka client to 3.6.x to pick up connection pooling/backpressure improvements. Run canary on a non-critical cluster before rolling to production.

Success criteria (acceptance):
- Tail latency (p95/p99) for small interactive requests reduced by >=30% during synthetic cross-tenant spike tests.
- CPU and GC cycles attributable to connection churn reduced by >=25% in benchmark harness.
- No regression in throughput under steady-state load.
- Rollout plan validated with canary traffic and automated rollback on error budget breach.

Risks and trade-offs:
- Gossip reduces central bottlenecks but can delay global coordination (eventual consistency). We'll bound TTL and combine with emergency centralized override.
- Library upgrades may expose API changes; test matrix includes our TLS/KMS integrations to catch regressions.

Acceptance tests and artifacts: see attachments for benchmark dashboards and PRs.

2026-02-28 - Marco Alvarez: Prototype complete. Local controller applies score computed from weighted recent pressure and queue-length derivative. Microbenchmark (single shard) shows 28% reduction in p99 under synthetic downstream delay (200ms added). PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/4512

2026-03-03 - QA (Priya Shah): Integration test added for cross-shard gossip flooding. Found a regression where extremely late TTL caused oscillation. Marco updated controller to use exponential backoff and clamped TTL to 3 intervals. Test dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/async/backpressure-20260303

2026-03-07 - Security (Evan Li): Verified client upgrade bundle against KMS integration; noted a required TLS cipher fallback for some legacy customer proxies. Added test to nightly matrix. See notes: https://docs.redwood.ai/security/compatibility#tls

2026-03-10 - Marco Alvarez: Canary started on cluster 'canary-us-west-2-a' with 10% of traffic. No errors in first 24h; observed 35% decrease in p99 for interactive route /generate-chat under injected downstream pauses. Leaving in canary for full 72h window before rolling to staged. Link to canary PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4987
